answer: Agents can earn voting weight only through a bonded reputation that grows when independent counterparties confirm useful work and survives a delay before payout. A ridge of scarce tasks makes identities compete for real demand; a mirror check links repeated claims to shared funding or behavior, so splitting one operator into many accounts does not multiply trust. The glacier is the slow release of rewards: an attacker must lock capital and sustain costly, verifiable activity across identities, while colluding accounts cannot cheaply manufacture independent confirmations.
